newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.

text.p: *Volume narrows to 8.022 bln from 10.361 bln pesos
Manila overnight money was steady at an average of 10.53125 percent on Wednesday, traders said.
Banks continued to remain liquid but rates did not fall since the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate had been maintained at 10.5 percent, they said.
Rates were wedged from 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent. The market had 22 lenders and 12 borrowers.
At the secondary market of T-bills and notes, dealers said the market experienced some lull after the frenzied buying of short-term bills on Tuesday.
"The buying on short-term bills was not as active as before," a big bank dealer said.
A Reuter poll of five banks showed them with bid rates ranging from 10.63 to 10.65 percent on the three-month bills.

But banks were tentative in pricing their long-term fixed-rate treasury bonds after the sharp fall in the coupon rate of the five-year T-bonds to 12.5 percent from 14.5 percent at Tuesday's auction, traders said.
